description: Intent-anchored eval scenarios for the Algolia connector. Mostly arrange-act coverage probes: the connector self-provisions its world (indices auto-create on first write) namespaced by {{run_id}}, exercises the capability, and cleans up. Post-write verification prefers getObject/getTask over search because Algolia indexing is asynchronous. Assertions split into outcome (backend-agnostic world/reply facts, graded on all arms) and mechanism (tool-call hygiene, our-arm-only).

evals.description: Add a record with a known objectID to a fresh index, retrieve it by id, then delete the index.

steps.intent: Add a record to the index 'eval-index-{{run_id}}' with objectID 'sku-1' and fields {"name":"Wireless Earbuds","price":79}.

outcome: A record with objectID 'sku-1' is added to the 'eval-index-{{run_id}}' index and a task id is reported.
mechanism: Sends the record with the caller-supplied objectID 'sku-1' rather than letting Algolia auto-generate one; the objectID is passed as a string.

steps.intent: Get the record with objectID 'sku-1' from 'eval-index-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: The record 'sku-1' is returned with name 'Wireless Earbuds' and price 79.
mechanism: Retrieves the record by its objectID directly rather than scanning or searching.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-index-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-index-{{run_id}}' index is deleted and a task id is reported (cleanup).

evals.description: Seed a couple of records, confirm indexing, then search with a query and a filter.

steps.intent: Add two records to 'eval-search-{{run_id}}': objectID 'a' {"title":"Red Shoes","inStock":true}, and objectID 'b' {"title":"Blue Hat","inStock":false}.

outcome: Both records ('a' and 'b') are added to the 'eval-search-{{run_id}}' index and a task id is reported.
mechanism: Adds both records with their caller-supplied objectIDs; may use a single batch call or two adds.

steps.intent: Wait until indexing for 'eval-search-{{run_id}}' has finished (the last write is published).

outcome: The prior write's task is confirmed published/applied for 'eval-search-{{run_id}}'.
mechanism: Checks task status for the index rather than assuming the write is instantly searchable.

steps.intent: Search 'eval-search-{{run_id}}' for 'shoes' returning only in-stock records.

outcome: The search returns the 'Red Shoes' record and not the out-of-stock 'Blue Hat', with a total-hits count reported.
mechanism: Passes the in-stock condition as a filter/facet parameter rather than filtering results client-side after retrieving everything.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-search-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-search-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Create a record, partial-update one attribute, and confirm the other attributes survive (partial update must not drop siblings).

steps.intent: Add a record to 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}' with objectID 'p1' and fields {"name":"Desk","price":100,"color":"oak"}.

outcome: A record 'p1' with name 'Desk', price 100, color 'oak' exists in 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}'.

steps.intent: Update only the price of record 'p1' in 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}' to 120.

outcome: Record 'p1' now has price 120.
mechanism: Uses a partial-update (patch) call that sends only the price attribute, not a full-record replace.

steps.intent: Get record 'p1' from 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}' and report all its fields.

outcome: Record 'p1' has price 120 and still has name 'Desk' and color 'oak' (the untouched attributes were preserved).

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-patch-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Bulk-index several records in one request, then confirm they landed by id.

steps.intent: Add these three records to 'eval-batch-{{run_id}}' in one operation: {"objectID":"1","n":"one"}, {"objectID":"2","n":"two"}, {"objectID":"3","n":"three"}.

outcome: All three records are indexed into 'eval-batch-{{run_id}}' and a task id (with the affected object ids) is reported.
mechanism: Uses a single batch operation rather than three separate add calls.

steps.intent: Retrieve records with objectIDs '1', '2', and '3' from 'eval-batch-{{run_id}}' in one request.

outcome: All three records are returned, each matching its objectID.
mechanism: Uses a single multi-get request rather than three separate gets.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-batch-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-batch-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Seed records and export the whole index via cursor browse (not paginated search).

steps.intent: Add two records to 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}': {"objectID":"x","v":1} and {"objectID":"y","v":2}, and wait for indexing to finish.

outcome: Both records are indexed into 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}' and the write is confirmed applied.

steps.intent: Export every record from 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: All records in 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}' (objectIDs 'x' and 'y') are returned.
mechanism: Uses the cursor browse capability for a full export rather than paginated search.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-browse-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Delete a subset of records by filter; the connector requires a non-empty filter.

steps.intent: Add to 'eval-delby-{{run_id}}': {"objectID":"keep","status":"active"} and {"objectID":"drop","status":"obsolete"}, and wait for indexing.

outcome: Both records are indexed into 'eval-delby-{{run_id}}' and the write is confirmed applied.

steps.intent: Delete all records in 'eval-delby-{{run_id}}' whose status is 'obsolete'.

outcome: The delete-by-filter operation is accepted for the obsolete records and a task id is reported; the 'keep' record is not targeted.
mechanism: Passes a non-empty filter selecting status:obsolete rather than an empty/match-all delete.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-delby-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-delby-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Empty an index of all records while keeping the index and its config.

steps.intent: Add {"objectID":"z","v":1} to 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' and wait for indexing.

outcome: The record is indexed into 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' and the write is confirmed applied.

steps.intent: Remove all records from 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' but keep the index.

outcome: All records are cleared from 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' and a task id is reported.
mechanism: Uses the clear-records capability, not delete-index and not an unfiltered delete-by-query.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-clear-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Make an attribute facetable via settings, then search its facet values.

steps.intent: Add to 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}': {"objectID":"1","brand":"Nike"}, {"objectID":"2","brand":"Nintendo"}, {"objectID":"3","brand":"Adidas"}.

outcome: The three records are indexed into 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}'.

steps.intent: Configure 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}' so that 'brand' can be faceted and searched as a facet.

outcome: The index settings now include 'brand' as a facetable (searchable-facet) attribute and a task id is reported.
mechanism: Updates the index settings' attributesForFaceting to include brand (as a searchable facet) rather than attempting to facet without configuring it.

steps.intent: In 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}', find brand facet values starting with 'ni'.

outcome: The facet-value search returns brand values matching 'ni' (Nike and Nintendo) and not Adidas.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-facet-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Set searchable attributes on an index and read them back.

steps.intent: Create the index 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}' by adding a record {"objectID":"1","title":"hi","body":"there"}.

outcome: The 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}' index exists with the record indexed.

steps.intent: Set the searchable attributes of 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}' to 'title' then 'body'.

outcome: The index settings update is accepted (searchable attributes set to title, then body) and a task id is reported.

steps.intent: Show the current settings of 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: The returned settings show searchableAttributes as ['title','body'].

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-settings-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Create a synonym, find it, and delete it.

steps.intent: Create the index 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}' by adding {"objectID":"1","name":"phone"}.

outcome: The 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}' index exists.

steps.intent: In 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}', create a synonym with id 'syn1' making 'phone', 'mobile', and 'cell' equivalent.

outcome: A synonym 'syn1' equating phone/mobile/cell is saved to 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}' and a task id is reported.

steps.intent: List the synonyms in 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: The synonym 'syn1' is returned with its equivalent terms.

steps.intent: Delete synonym 'syn1' from 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}', then delete the index.

outcome: The 'syn1' synonym is deleted and the 'eval-syn-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Create a query rule, search for it, and delete it.

steps.intent: Create the index 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}' by adding {"objectID":"1","name":"widget"}.

outcome: The 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}' index exists.

steps.intent: In 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}', create a query rule with id 'rule1' that fires when the query is 'promo' and applies a simple consequence.

outcome: A query rule 'rule1' is saved to 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}' and a task id is reported.
mechanism: Saves a single rule with a consequence; does not require batch.

steps.intent: List the query rules in 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: The rule 'rule1' is returned.

steps.intent: Delete rule 'rule1' from 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}', then delete the index.

outcome: The 'rule1' rule is deleted and the 'eval-rule-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: List the application's indices (read-only against ambient state).

steps.intent: List the Algolia indices in this application and report how many there are.

outcome: A list of the application's indices is returned, each with a name (and record count where available).
mechanism: Uses the list-indices capability rather than guessing index names.

evals.description: After a write, confirm it was applied via task status (async indexing).

steps.intent: Add {"objectID":"t1","v":1} to 'eval-task-{{run_id}}' and then confirm the write has actually been applied (not just accepted).

outcome: The record write is confirmed applied/published for 'eval-task-{{run_id}}' (not merely acknowledged).
mechanism: Checks the returned task id's status until it is published rather than assuming immediate consistency.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-task-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-task-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Request related-product recommendations for a record. The Recommend model is likely untrained, so an empty result is the valid, graceful outcome — the point is the tool is called correctly and empty is handled, not that recommendations exist.

steps.intent: Add a record to 'eval-rec-{{run_id}}' with objectID 'demo-1' and fields {"name":"Blue Sneakers","category":"shoes"}, and wait for indexing.

outcome: The record 'demo-1' is indexed into 'eval-rec-{{run_id}}' and the write is confirmed applied.

steps.intent: Get related-product recommendations for objectID 'demo-1' in 'eval-rec-{{run_id}}'.

outcome: A recommendations result is returned for 'demo-1' — a possibly-empty list of recommended records; if the model has no trained data the reply conveys that none are available rather than erroring out or fabricating results.
mechanism: Calls the recommendations capability with the related-products model and objectID 'demo-1'.

steps.intent: Delete the 'eval-rec-{{run_id}}' index.

outcome: The 'eval-rec-{{run_id}}' index is deleted (cleanup).

evals.description: Graceful refusal: managing Algolia API keys is out of scope for this connector.

steps.intent: Create a new search-only Algolia API key restricted to the 'products' index.

outcome: The reply states that creating or managing Algolia API keys is not supported by this connector (pointing to the Algolia dashboard) and does not claim a key was created.
mechanism: Does not call any tool to fabricate key creation.
